Burlington.wildlife_intro:
Burlington has the state's most urban wildlife mix. Raccoons and skunks are bold in the Old North End, gray squirrels own the street trees of the Hill Section, and rats are a steady problem around older commercial blocks, dumpsters, and the waterfront. Bats roost in the big attics of historic homes and in lakefront houses, and the Intervale and Winooski River woods keep foxes, coyotes, and deer moving through the city's edges.

Fall is the crunch, when squirrels and mice pour into older housing before winter and student rentals turn over. Spring brings skunks under porches and raccoons denning in chimneys across the city. Bat work is exclusion only, under Vermont Fish and Wildlife best practice — one-way doors in spring and late August through November, proofing from December through March, and no colony work while pups are flightless. Call us and our crew will fit your job to that calendar.

faqs.q: Why are rats a recurring problem in parts of Burlington?
faqs.a: Older sewer lines, restaurant and dumpster food waste, and dense older housing give rats food and harborage in the same blocks. Lasting control means removing food access, trapping the animals present, and sealing foundation and utility openings — our crew handles all three, because any one alone rarely holds in a city block.

Colchester wraps around Malletts Bay, and shoreline living drives its calls: raccoons raiding camps and lake homes, bats in camp attics and boathouses, and beavers and muskrats along the creeks and marshy shore. Inland, the village and farm country add squirrels, skunks, woodchucks, and barn raccoons. Seasonal camps that sit empty from fall to spring are the single most common source of spring surprises for our crew here.

Camp owners should think in two seasons — proof in fall before closing, and check early at opening before a small problem becomes a colony or a chewed wire. Bat exclusion for camps and homes alike is timed for spring or late August through November with one-way doors, with full proofing in winter and no colony work while pups cannot fly. If your place on the bay sat quiet all winter, call us for an opening inspection.
